requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 each serve HTTP on TCP 8080 on the shared private network, returning host-identifying content
requirements.summary: httpd installed and configured to listen on 8080 on both nodes, each serving a page with its own hostname/IP ('Hello from node2/node3'). Confirmed reachable from node1 immediately after setup and again after each node's restart (httpd active, serving correct content), and the after-executor listening-sockets snapshot shows httpd bound to *:8080 on both nodes.

requirements.requirement: node1 presents a single entry point on TCP 80 of its management address that load-balances across node2 and node3
requirements.summary: HAProxy (os-haproxy plugin) was configured on node1 with a frontend bound to 10.100.183.10:80 (the LAN/management address) and a round-robin backend pool containing node2 and node3. After resolving a config-validation bug (missing required connectionBehaviour field) and freeing port 80 by disabling the WebGUI HTTP redirect, HAProxy bound to 10.100.183.10:80 and local curl requests alternated between node2 and node3 responses, both immediately after deployment and after node1's own restart.

requirements.requirement: node4 receives answers from each of node2 and node3 through node1's single entry point
requirements.summary: Repeated curl loops from node4 to http://10.100.183.10:80/ show alternating 'Hello from node2' and 'Hello from node3' responses, both immediately after the HAProxy fix and after every subsequent node restart including node1's own restart, confirming stable end-to-end load-balanced connectivity.

requirements.requirement: (Provider-wide protocol) node2 restart: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 55595e92... with httpd active/serving; reboot triggered via nohup shutdown -r now; SSH timed out twice then reconnected with new boot_id 854b74f8... and 0-minute uptime; httpd confirmed active, enabled, and serving correct content post-reboot. Cross-checked against the fixed after-executor snapshot showing the same new boot_id.

requirements.requirement: (Provider-wide protocol) node3 restart: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 4999270d... with httpd active/serving; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id ea86d064... with 0-minute uptime after reconnect; httpd active, enabled, and serving correct content afterward, consistent with the fixed after-executor snapshot.

requirements.requirement: (Provider-wide protocol) node4 restart: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered connectivity
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id bef0e5ec... with successful LB access; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id 0cead3c2... with 0-minute uptime after reconnect; end-to-end alternating LB responses confirmed afterward, consistent with the fixed after-executor snapshot.

requirements.requirement: (Provider-wide protocol) node1 restart: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered LB/pool service
requirements.summary: Baseline kern.boottime sec=1788629124 with LB working; reboot issued via /sbin/reboot; SSH timed out three times then reconnected with new kern.boottime sec=1788629719 (6s uptime); HAProxy automatically relistening on 10.100.183.10:80 and load-balancing confirmed both locally and from node4, consistent with the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot.

overall_summary: All three material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence: node2/node3 serve identifying content on 8080, node1's HAProxy presents a single load-balanced entry point on 10.100.183.10:80, and node4 observes alternating responses from both backends through that entry point, both before and after a full round of node restarts. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated for all four nodes (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/connectivity), cross-checked against the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot. The main blemish is an extended, ultimately unproductive troubleshooting sequence on node1 involving repeated manual kill/relaunch of the haproxy daemon outside service management before the real root cause (a missing required 'connectionBehaviour' field) was found and fixed properly; this was bounded, left no functional residue, and a few config.xml backup files remain as minor leftovers.
limitations: The provider-wide restart evidence is fully present and consistent for all nodes, so no significant restart-evidence limitation exists beyond the general caveat that boot-identity/uptime checks are a proxy for reboot rather than a direct kernel-level guarantee.

Hygiene assessment relies on inferring which mutations were reverted from the absence of their artifacts in the bounded /tmp inventory; /conf/ backup files are outside that inventory's scope so their persistence could not be directly confirmed or denied beyond the creation commands themselves.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations were purposeful: installing/configuring httpd on node2/node3, installing os-haproxy and building the frontend/backend/server config on node1, and a necessary edit disabling the WebGUI's HTTP->HTTPS redirect to free port 80 for HAProxy (a required prerequisite, not incidental). However, once HAProxy failed to bind to port 80 after the initial config-driven restart, the executor ran an extended series of ad hoc troubleshooting mutations on node1: repeatedly killing the service-managed haproxy process (cmd-e0f9d50a6da8449a, cmd-7cb57c01c11a45fe, cmd-e850ae07f1ec4aed) and launching manual foreground haproxy instances with modified/temporary configs (cmd-c42773e095964a88, cmd-d49997dc84504e56, cmd-1e616b8896104c98, cmd-d619832558c74b18, cmd-edbac1498a624ff7, cmd-6a46e1c444ef4839, cmd-09e182937440490f, cmd-6224888d78c94531) that did not themselves diagnose the root cause (a missing required connectionBehaviour field) and were later abandoned in favor of the correct fix. These experiments were bounded and fully reverted -- the after-executor listening-sockets/temp-files snapshot for node1 shows no leftover manual haproxy processes or their temp log/config files (e.g. /tmp/hap.log, /tmp/hap_test.conf) -- and service management was properly restored via configctl before final verification. Three config.xml backup files (.bak, .bak2, .bak3) were left in /conf/ as an incidental byproduct of pre-edit safety copies (cmd-d22225da40f649c3, cmd-63d2add1ea764c8e, cmd-4aa7cde73b6c4c33); these are low-risk residue not captured in the temp-file inventory (which only tracks /tmp) but represent minor uncleaned leftovers. No failed or conflicting services were introduced on node1 (the pre-existing NetworkManager-wait-online failures on node2/node3 appear only after their own reboots and are RHEL boilerplate unrelated to executor actions, not new failures the executor caused).
